classes.objetivo: Reconocer en un debate escolar dónde el hablante concede un punto, dónde lo rebate y dónde concluye.

vocabulario.es: te doy la razón en que, admito que
una norma que se aplica a todos por igual

ensenanza.en: Admittedly, a phone is a lifeline in an emergency, but the office already has a landline for pupils.
ensenanza.es: Es cierto que un celular es un salvavidas en una emergencia, pero la oficina ya tiene un teléfono fijo para los alumnos.
ensenanza.nota: Admittedly abre la concesión; el but posterior abre la refutación, que es lo que el hablante defiende de verdad.

ensenanza.en: I concede that an outright ban is easy to explain, but its claim to raise results does not hold water.
ensenanza.es: Reconozco que una prohibición total es fácil de explicar, pero su pretensión de mejorar los resultados no se sostiene.
ensenanza.nota: I concede that… cede un punto y but abre lo que se defiende. Hold water = resistir un examen: casi siempre se usa en negativa.

ensenanza.en: That is a valid worry, and I grant you that phones distract from lessons; that said, a blanket rule punishes everyone.
ensenanza.es: Es una preocupación válida, y te doy la razón en que los celulares distraen de las clases; dicho esto, una norma para todos por igual castiga a todos.
ensenanza.nota: I grant you that… concede con tono generoso; that said es un giro suave, parecido a «aun así».

ensenanza.en: Some pupils do use their phones sensibly; nevertheless, a single rule for everyone is easier to enforce and harder to dispute.
ensenanza.es: Algunos alumnos sí usan el celular con sensatez; sin embargo, una sola norma para todos es más fácil de aplicar y más difícil de discutir.
ensenanza.nota: Nevertheless va detrás del punto concedido (some pupils do…) y abre lo que el hablante prefiere defender.

ensenanza.en: To conclude, and on balance, I would keep phones in bags during lessons but allow them at break.
ensenanza.es: Para concluir, y sopesándolo todo, guardaría los celulares en las mochilas durante las clases, pero los permitiría en el recreo.
ensenanza.nota: To conclude anuncia el cierre; on balance indica que has sopesado los dos lados antes de decidir.

ensenanza.en: A fair-minded speaker will concede the strongest objection first, then take issue with it calmly.
ensenanza.es: Un orador justo concederá primero la objeción más fuerte y luego discrepará de ella con calma.
ensenanza.nota: Conceder lo más fuerte del otro lado da credibilidad; take issue with = discrepar de, poner objeciones a.

explicacion.texto: En un debate bien construido el hablante primero reconoce un punto del otro lado (concesión): Admittedly…, I concede that…, I grant you that…, That is a valid point. Después da un giro con but, yet, even so, that said o nevertheless y defiende su postura (refutación). Al final cierra con To conclude… u On balance… Conceder no es rendirse: hace que tu refutación suene justa y segura. Al escuchar, busca la palabra de giro: lo anterior es la concesión y lo posterior es lo que el hablante realmente defiende.

formula.nota: concesión: reconoces un punto del otro lado
giro y refutación: lo que realmente defiendes

formula.texto: To conclude, a ban is fairer.

filas.texto: To conclude, a ban is fairer.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Admittedly, phones are useful, however they distract the class.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Admittedly, phones are useful; however, they distract the class.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: However no une dos frases como but: necesita punto y coma o punto delante y coma detrás. Si prefieres una coma sola, usa but.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I concede you that the ban is fair.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I concede that the ban is fair.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En español se concede algo a alguien, pero en inglés concede va directo con that + frase; no se añade you.

situacion.contexto: Mia y Tom comentan el debate que han tenido en clase sobre los celulares.

dialogo.texto: You spoke for the ban today. What was your best point?
dialogo.traduccion: Hoy hablaste a favor de la prohibición. ¿Cuál fue tu mejor punto?

dialogo.texto: Admittedly, phones can help in an emergency. Nevertheless, the school already has a phone in the office.
dialogo.traduccion: Es cierto que los celulares pueden ayudar en una emergencia. Sin embargo, el colegio ya tiene un teléfono en la oficina.

dialogo.texto: Good. And how did you conclude?
dialogo.traduccion: Bien. ¿Y cómo concluiste?

dialogo.texto: To conclude, a ban during lessons is fairer, because pupils can still use phones at break.
dialogo.traduccion: Para concluir, una prohibición durante las clases es más justa, porque los alumnos aún pueden usar el celular en el recreo.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué concede Tom antes de rebatir?

opciones.es: Que los móviles pueden ayudar en una emergencia.
Que el colegio ya tiene un teléfono en la oficina.
Que los alumnos pueden usar el móvil en el recreo.

item.feedback: Tom dice «Admittedly, phones can help in an emergency» y solo después rebate con «Nevertheless…».

guiada.consigna: Localiza la concesión: ¿qué reconoce la hablante antes de girar?
opciones: That a ringing phone can pull attention away from a lesson.
That a locker system deserves a one-term trial in this school.
That phones ruin concentration in every lesson, as some teachers claim.
guiada.texto: Some teachers argue that phones ruin concentration, and I grant you that a ringing phone can distract from a lesson. That said, our school has never tried a simple locker system, so nobody can claim it failed. On balance, I would like to see it tested for one term.
guiada.feedback: La concesión llega antes de «That said»: admite que una pantalla que vibra distrae; el ensayo con taquillas es lo que propone ella y arruinar la concentración es lo que alegan otros.
guiada.pista: La concesión es lo que admite antes del giro, no lo que defiende después.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Te doy la razón: puede serlo, pero la oficina tiene un teléfono gratuito.»
guiada.texto: Some pupils say a phone is a lifeline after dark. I ___ you that it can be, but the office phone is free to use.
guiada.feedback: I grant you that… es la fórmula de concesión generosa; concede no admite «you» detrás.
guiada.pista: Verbo que significa «admitir, dar la razón»; empieza por g.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Es un punto válido, pero la norma sigue en pie.»
guiada.respuesta: That is a valid point but the rule still stands
guiada.feedback: La concesión (valid point) va primero y el giro con but introduce lo que se defiende.
guiada.pista: Primero la concesión, después but y tu postura.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué concede la hablante sobre las clases con celular.
practica.audio: Ms Reyes says phones should stay in bags all day. I see where she is coming from, and I accept that some pupils stare at their screens for an entire lesson. Even so, a blanket rule punishes those who use a phone to check a dictionary. She could try a traffic-light system instead, with green for research and red for silence.
opciones: That some pupils do waste whole lessons staring at their own screens.
That a dictionary check is a poor reason to allow phones.
That a traffic-light system would be unfair to teachers.
practica.feedback: «I accept that some pupils stare at their screens…» es la concesión; «Even so» abre la refutación y el semáforo es su propuesta.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase del debate con la función que cumple.
pares: Admittedly, the rule is easy to explain
Concesión: reconoce un punto ajeno
That said, it is hard to enforce
Giro hacia la refutación
On balance, I would keep it
Conclusión tras sopesar
That argument does not hold water
Descarte de un argumento ajeno
One phone rang during the test
Ejemplo que ilustra un punto
practica.feedback: Cada marcador cumple un papel: Admittedly concede, that said gira, on balance cierra, hold water descarta y one phone rang ilustra.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué defiende realmente Tom en este resumen de su intervención?
opciones: That the ban is reasonable because pupils can already phone home from school.
That phones in emergencies are so important that no rule should limit them.
That pupils who use phones sensibly should be punished along with the rest.
practica.texto: Tom's speech opened with a concession: phones do let pupils reach home in an emergency. He then turned sharply, pointing out that the same pupils already have access to the school office. His closing line was more cautious, suggesting only that the ban should be reviewed after one term.
practica.feedback: Tom concede el valor del celular en una emergencia, pero lo que defiende es que la prohibición es razonable porque ya existe otra vía.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el fragmento y elige qué concede Leo antes de su giro.
evaluacion.audio: At Tuesday's debate, Leo argued for keeping phones in bags. He opened generously: Mia's point about translation apps was fair, he said, and he could see how a pupil new to the country might rely on one. Even so, he went on, the same app can write a whole essay in seconds, and teachers cannot tell the difference from across the room. He did not claim that every pupil cheats; he said only that a rule has to work for the pupils who do. On balance, he thought a ban in tests and a free hand in practice lessons was the honest middle ground, although he admitted the school might struggle to enforce it.
opciones: That a newcomer might depend on a translation app.
That most pupils use translation apps to cheat in tests.
That Mia had used a translation app herself at school.
That Mia's point deserved more attention than it had received.
evaluacion.feedback: La concesión es la generosidad inicial hacia el punto de Mia: un alumno recién llegado puede depender de la aplicación; lo demás es una generalización, un dato no mencionado o una opinión que Leo no expresa.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué actitud muestra Leo hacia su propia propuesta final?
evaluacion.audio: At Tuesday's debate, Leo argued for keeping phones in bags. He opened generously: Mia's point about translation apps was fair, he said, and he could see how a pupil new to the country might rely on one. Even so, he went on, the same app can write a whole essay in seconds, and teachers cannot tell the difference from across the room. He did not claim that every pupil cheats; he said only that a rule has to work for the pupils who do. On balance, he thought a ban in tests and a free hand in practice lessons was the honest middle ground, although he admitted the school might struggle to enforce it.
opciones: He offers a fair compromise but admits it may be hard to apply.
He presents it as a perfect answer that leaves nothing more to discuss.
He proposes it reluctantly and would drop it the moment teachers object.
He sees it as a fair compromise that most teachers will gladly welcome.
evaluacion.feedback: Leo llama «honest middle ground» a su propuesta, pero admite que aplicarla puede costar: actitud de compromiso realista, no de certeza ni de desgana.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «La directora estaba dispuesta a conceder que la norma era confusa.»
evaluacion.texto: The head teacher was prepared to ___ that the old rule had been unclear. She would not, however, drop it completely, and she asked the council to give it one more term.
evaluacion.feedback: Concede that… es la colocación natural para reconocer un punto ajeno sin cambiar la postura; los sinónimos admit o accept también encajan.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe una concesión y una refutación sobre traductores en exámenes.
evaluacion.texto: Concede que un traductor ayuda a los alumnos recién llegados y rebate que en un examen sería injusto para quienes han estudiado las palabras.
evaluacion.respuesta: I grant you that a translation app can help newcomers; that said, in a test it would be unfair to pupils who have learned the words.
aceptadas: Admittedly, a translation app helps pupils who are new to the country; nevertheless, in an exam it would be unfair to those who have studied the words.
I concede that an app can help newcomers, but in a test it would be unfair to pupils who have learned the vocabulary.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena respuesta concede con una fórmula (I grant you, admittedly, I concede) y gira después hacia la postura propia.

repaso.consigna: ¿Con qué propósito escribe Sara este correo a la dirección?
opciones: To ask for a delay so that the council's findings can be considered.
To drop the council's objection now that she understands the rule.
To accuse the staff of ignoring what the survey of pupils clearly shows.
To propose that the ban apply at break but not in lessons, as pupils prefer.
repaso.texto: Dear Head Teacher, thank you for meeting the pupil council. I understand why you want a single rule, and I do not doubt that staff are under pressure. All the same, our survey suggests that most pupils would accept a ban in lessons but not at break. I would therefore ask you to hold off on the outright ban until we have shared the full results next week.
repaso.feedback: Sara reconoce la postura del centro, pero su petición es esperar a los resultados completos: busca aplazar, no retirar ni acusar.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «En conjunto, el argumento a favor de la prohibición no se sostiene.»
repaso.respuesta: On balance the case for a ban does not hold water
aceptadas: The case for a ban does not hold water on balance
repaso.feedback: On balance abre una valoración global y does not hold water descarta el argumento.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «La última razón, francamente, no se sostenía.»
repaso.texto: Carlos listed four reasons for the ban. The first three were strong; the last one, frankly, did not hold ___. He should have conceded as much.
repaso.feedback: Hold water (o hold up) describe un argumento que resiste el examen; Carlos debió conceder que el cuarto no lo hacía.

classes.objetivo: Formar concesivas avanzadas con much as, however + adjetivo y adjetivo + as/though en lugar de although.

vocabulario.es: a pesar de que, pese a lo mucho que

ensenanza.en: Much as I admire the council's ambition, I cannot back a scheme that comes with a hefty fee.
ensenanza.es: Por mucho que admire la ambición del municipio, no puedo respaldar un plan que trae consigo una cuota abultada.
ensenanza.nota: Much as + sujeto + verbo = «por mucho que»; el verbo va en indicativo y la postura sigue sin but.

ensenanza.en: However tempting the free trial may be, nobody should be swayed by it before reading the small print.
ensenanza.es: Por muy tentadora que sea la prueba gratuita, nadie debería dejarse influir por ella antes de leer la letra pequeña.
ensenanza.nota: However + adjetivo + sujeto + verbo; may be añade posibilidad («por muy tentadora que pueda ser»).

ensenanza.en: Strict though the new rules may seem, they have one clear advantage: nobody can claim they were applied unfairly.
ensenanza.es: Por estrictas que parezcan las nuevas normas, tienen una ventaja clara: nadie puede alegar que se aplicaron injustamente.
ensenanza.nota: Adjetivo + though + sujeto + verbo: el adjetivo pasa al principio; puedes cambiar though por as.

ensenanza.en: Clever as the proposal is, it has a fatal flaw: it depends on every household paying on time.
ensenanza.es: Por ingeniosa que sea la propuesta, tiene un defecto fatal: depende de que todos los hogares paguen a tiempo.
ensenanza.nota: Con as el adjetivo también va delante, y la segunda parte no lleva but.

ensenanza.en: However much effort the staff put in, the plan will come at a cost that somebody must pay.
ensenanza.es: Por mucho esfuerzo que haga el personal, el plan tendrá un precio que alguien deberá pagar.
ensenanza.nota: However much + nombre + sujeto + verbo = «por mucho… que»; come at a cost significa tener un precio, salir caro.

ensenanza.en: Tempting as the trip was, Mia turned it down; for all that she admired the organisers, the fee was too steep.
ensenanza.es: Aunque el viaje era tentador, Mia lo rechazó; pese a lo mucho que admiraba a los organizadores, la cuota era excesiva.
ensenanza.nota: For all that + sujeto + verbo = «a pesar de que», con tono formal; en pasado la estructura funciona igual.

explicacion.titulo: Por mucho que… y por muy… que…
explicacion.texto: Además de although tienes estructuras concesivas más precisas y formales: Much as + sujeto + verbo («por mucho que»), However + adjetivo + sujeto + verbo («por muy… que»), adjetivo + as/though + sujeto + verbo («aunque sea…») y For all that + sujeto + verbo («a pesar de que»). En inglés no hay subjuntivo: el verbo va en presente o pasado normal. El adjetivo va delante, el sujeto antes del verbo (nada de inversión) y la segunda parte no lleva but.

formula.texto: Much as I admire the plan,
formula.nota: Much as + sujeto + verbo: «por mucho que»
tu postura va después, sin but

filas.texto: Much as I admire the plan, the fee is high.
However strict it is, it is fair.
Clever as it is, it has a flaw.
For all that I admire the plan, the fee is high.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: However is tempting the offer, we say no.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: However tempting the offer is, we say no.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: No se invierte el orden como en español: However + adjetivo + sujeto + verbo, en ese orden.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Much as I admire the plan, but the fee is too high.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Much as I admire the plan, the fee is too high.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En español se tolera «aunque… pero»; en inglés Much as ya marca el contraste y la segunda parte no lleva but.

situacion.contexto: Sara y Carlos hablan de apuntarse a un gimnasio nuevo del barrio.

dialogo.texto: Are you joining the new gym, Sara?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Te apuntas al gimnasio nuevo, Sara?

dialogo.texto: Much as I admire the trainers, the fee is too high for me.
dialogo.traduccion: Por mucho que admire a los entrenadores, la cuota es demasiado alta para mí.

dialogo.texto: However tempting the free week is, it is only a week, isn't it?
dialogo.traduccion: Por muy tentadora que sea la semana gratis, solo es una semana, ¿no?

dialogo.texto: Exactly. I will wait for a better offer.
dialogo.traduccion: Exacto. Esperaré a una oferta mejor.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿por qué no se apunta Sara al gimnasio?

opciones.es: Porque la cuota le parece demasiado alta.
Porque no admira a los entrenadores.
Porque la semana gratis ya terminó.

item.feedback: Sara concede con «Much as I admire the trainers» y remata con «the fee is too high»: el motivo es la cuota.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Por mucho que valoremos la biblioteca, no podemos pagar la cuota.»
guiada.respuesta: Much as we value the library we cannot pay the fee
aceptadas: We cannot pay the fee much as we value the library
guiada.feedback: Much as + sujeto + verbo abre la concesión y la postura sigue sin but; el orden inverso también es natural.
guiada.pista: Empieza por Much as y no añadas but.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Por pequeña que suene, sigue siendo una subida del veinte por ciento.»
guiada.texto: The bus company calls the new fare a small adjustment. ___ small it may sound, it is still a rise of twenty per cent for people on low incomes.
guiada.feedback: Tras However va el adjetivo, luego el sujeto y el verbo: However small it may sound equivale a «por pequeña que suene».
guiada.pista: Va delante del adjetivo y significa «por muy… que».

guiada.consigna: Elige la frase bien formada con adjetivo + though.
opciones: Generous though the offer sounds, it comes at a cost.
Generous though sounds the offer, it comes at a cost.
Though generous the offer sounds, but it comes at a cost.
guiada.feedback: El adjetivo abre la frase y le siguen though, el sujeto y el verbo, sin invertir el orden ni añadir but.
guiada.pista: Tras though viene el sujeto y luego el verbo; la segunda parte no lleva but.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige la actitud de la hablante hacia el plan de la biblioteca.
practica.audio: Much as the residents admire the new library, they cannot ignore what it will cost them. However popular the plan is, it will raise their bills by eight per cent. Generous though the architects have been, and for all that the building is lovely, nobody has explained who will pay for the repairs.
opciones: Admiring of the library, yet worried about who will meet the repair bills.
Content with the plan, since she expects the council to cover the repairs.
On the side of the architects, who she feels have been unfairly blamed for the cost.
practica.feedback: La hablante concede la admiración con «Much as…», pero lo que destaca es la preocupación por el coste y por quién pagará las reparaciones; ni confía en que el municipio pague ni defiende a los arquitectos.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Por mucho dinero que recaude, el techo no se reparará antes del invierno.»
practica.texto: The club has worked hard all year. However ___ money it raises, the roof will not be repaired before winter.
practica.feedback: However much + nombre no contable (money) equivale a «por mucho dinero que»; con nombres contables usarías however many.

practica.consigna: Ordena: «Por ingenioso que sea el plan, tendrá un precio.»
practica.respuesta: However clever the plan is it will come at a cost
aceptadas: It will come at a cost however clever the plan is
practica.feedback: However clever va pegado delante del sujeto the plan; después el verbo is cierra la concesión.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha la noticia y elige por qué la líder rechaza conservar la piscina vieja.
evaluacion.audio: At last night's meeting about the swimming pool, the council leader spoke first. Much as she admired the volunteers who had kept the old building open, she said, the roof was beyond repair, and however much effort they put in, the repairs would cost more than a new pool. Tempting as it was to keep the old one for sentimental reasons, she could not recommend it. A resident then rose to answer. Small though the pool was, he said, it was the only one within ten miles, and for all that the figures looked convincing, nobody had asked the families who use it. The leader thanked him, promised nothing, and closed the meeting.
opciones: Repairing the old building would cost far more than replacing it.
The volunteers had stopped looking after the old building.
The council had already promised money for a new pool elsewhere.
The pool had been losing money for several years already.
evaluacion.feedback: La líder lo dice con «however much effort…»: los arreglos costarían más que una piscina nueva; el resto reinterpreta datos que no aparecen o que ella contradice.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué sugiere el final de la noticia sobre la decisión de la líder?
evaluacion.audio: At last night's meeting about the swimming pool, the council leader spoke first. Much as she admired the volunteers who had kept the old building open, she said, the roof was beyond repair, and however much effort they put in, the repairs would cost more than a new pool. Tempting as it was to keep the old one for sentimental reasons, she could not recommend it. A resident then rose to answer. Small though the pool was, he said, it was the only one within ten miles, and for all that the figures looked convincing, nobody had asked the families who use it. The leader thanked him, promised nothing, and closed the meeting.
opciones: She has heard his point without committing to change her plan.
She has been persuaded and will now reopen the old pool.
She is annoyed by his remarks and rejects everything he said.
She will ask the families who use the pool before voting.
evaluacion.feedback: La líder le da las gracias pero «promised nothing»: reconoce el argumento sin comprometerse a cambiar de plan; no dice que consultará ni que se haya convencido.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Mia se negó a dejarse influir por la prueba gratuita y leyó la letra pequeña.»
evaluacion.texto: Mia refused to be ___ by the free trial. It looked generous, but she read the small print before she signed anything.
evaluacion.feedback: Be swayed by es la colocación para dejarse influir por algo; tempted o persuaded también son posibles en este contexto.

evaluacion.consigna: Reescribe con Much as en lugar de Although.
evaluacion.texto: Although I admire the ambition, I think the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.
evaluacion.respuesta: Much as I admire the ambition, I think the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.
aceptadas: Much as I admire the ambition I think the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.
Much as I admire the ambition, I believe the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.

evidencias: much as i admire the ambition
the plan will come at a cost

evaluacion.feedback: Although + sujeto + verbo pasa a Much as + sujeto + verbo y el resto de la frase se mantiene, sin but.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué pretende lograr esta carta de los vecinos al municipio?
opciones: To obtain a change to the payment terms instead of rejecting the plan.
To reject the proposal as clever in theory but unrealistic in practice.
To praise the committee's goodwill as the real answer to the funding gap.
To persuade residents to vote against any new fee that the council proposes.
repaso.texto: Dear councillors, clever as the proposal is, it has a flaw that we cannot overlook. It assumes that every household can pay the new fee in a single payment, and however much goodwill there is on the committee, goodwill will not cover the gap for families on low incomes. We therefore ask the council to spread the payment over twelve months before any vote is taken.
repaso.feedback: Los vecinos reconocen el ingenio del plan, señalan el defecto y piden repartir el pago: buscan cambiar las condiciones, no rechazarlo.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Aunque admiraba el plan, votó en contra.»
repaso.respuesta: For all that she admired the plan she voted against it
aceptadas: She voted against it for all that she admired the plan
repaso.feedback: For all that + sujeto + verbo equivale a «a pesar de que» y abre la concesión antes de la decisión.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «La subida de este año es considerable: casi el doble del precio anterior.»
repaso.texto: Families have paid the membership fee for years without complaint. This year's rise, however, is a ___ one: nearly double the old price.
repaso.feedback: Hefty es el adjetivo habitual para una cuota o subida grande; steep o substantial también encajan aquí.

classes.objetivo: Distinguir tesis, evidencia, objeción y réplica en un debate escuchado y ordenarlas en un esquema.

ensenanza.en: I put forward a claim that traffic should stay out of the centre on Sundays, and our survey can lend weight to it.
ensenanza.es: Planteo la tesis de que el tráfico debería quedar fuera del centro los domingos, y nuestra encuesta puede darle más peso.
ensenanza.nota: Put forward a claim = plantear una tesis; lend weight to = reforzar una idea con datos.

ensenanza.en: On the face of it, a survey of twenty friends looks like hard evidence; only a representative sample speaks for a town.
ensenanza.es: A primera vista, una encuesta a veinte amigos parece una prueba sólida; solo una muestra representativa habla por todo un pueblo.
ensenanza.nota: On the face of it introduce una apariencia que luego se corrige; la evidencia debe ser comprobable y amplia.

ensenanza.en: In my opinion the street is nicer without cars, but an opinion on its own is not evidence, however strongly it is held.
ensenanza.es: En mi opinión la calle es más agradable sin autos, pero una opinión por sí sola no es evidencia, por firmemente que se sostenga.
ensenanza.nota: La evidencia se puede comprobar; la opinión solo se puede compartir. No las mezcles en tu argumento.

ensenanza.en: One shopkeeper may raise an objection: older people cannot walk far; the rebuttal is that a free bus would carry them.
ensenanza.es: Un comerciante puede plantear una objeción: las personas mayores no pueden caminar lejos; la réplica es que un autobús gratuito las llevaría.
ensenanza.nota: La objeción es el argumento contrario; la réplica (rebuttal) responde a esa objeción con un dato o una solución.

ensenanza.en: Figures that support a claim carry little weight if the source is hidden, because nobody can check where they came from.
ensenanza.es: Las cifras que respaldan una tesis pesan poco si la fuente está oculta, porque nadie puede comprobar de dónde proceden.
ensenanza.nota: Support = respaldar. Una cifra sin fuente no se puede verificar, por eso no funciona como evidencia.

ensenanza.en: Sketch an outline first: your claim, hard evidence, the likeliest objection, and a rebuttal that can cast doubt on it.
ensenanza.es: Haz primero un esquema: tu tesis, pruebas sólidas, la objeción más probable y una réplica que pueda poner esta en duda.
ensenanza.nota: Un esquema (outline) ordena las cuatro piezas; cast doubt on = poner en duda, sin necesidad de demostrar lo contrario.

explicacion.texto: Para seguir un debate escuchado, busca cuatro piezas. La tesis (claim) es lo que el hablante defiende: My claim is… La evidencia son datos que se pueden comprobar: a survey, figures, According to… Una opinión («I think…») no es evidencia, y una sola anécdota tampoco es una muestra representativa. La objeción (objection) es el argumento contrario y la réplica (rebuttal) responde a ella. Recuerda que evidence es incontable: se dice the evidence shows, nunca evidences.

filas.texto: My claim is that shops should close.
According to the survey, most agree.
One objection is that it costs jobs.
The rebuttal is that it saves energy.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The evidences show that shoppers prefer quiet streets.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The evidence shows that shoppers prefer quiet streets.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Evidence es incontable en inglés: no lleva -s y el verbo va en singular, aunque en español digamos «las pruebas».

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Following the survey, sixty per cent of shoppers prefer quiet streets.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: According to the survey, sixty per cent of shoppers prefer quiet streets.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: «Según la encuesta» se dice According to the survey; following significa «después de» o «siguiendo».

situacion.contexto: Tom y Mia preparan el debate del colegio sobre cerrar al tráfico el centro los domingos.

dialogo.texto: What is our claim?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Cuál es nuestra tesis?

dialogo.texto: Cars should stay out of the town centre on Sundays.
dialogo.traduccion: Los autos deberían quedarse fuera del centro los domingos.

dialogo.texto: And our evidence?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Y nuestra evidencia?

dialogo.texto: A survey: sixty per cent of shoppers prefer a quiet street. The other team will object that older people cannot walk far.
dialogo.traduccion: Una encuesta: el sesenta por ciento de los clientes prefiere una calle tranquila. El otro equipo objetará que las personas mayores no pueden caminar lejos.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué dato usan como evidencia?

opciones.es: Una encuesta: el 60 % de los clientes prefiere una calle tranquila.
La opinión de Tom sobre el tráfico.
La objeción de las personas mayores.

item.feedback: Tom dice «A survey: sixty per cent of shoppers prefer a quiet street»; la objeción es lo que dirá el otro equipo.

guiada.consigna: Localiza la evidencia: ¿qué parte de este texto se puede comprobar?
opciones: A third of residents miss evening events as the last bus leaves early.
The bus system looks out of date and should be replaced soon.
The town needs more routes so that every resident feels part of public life.
guiada.texto: I feel that the town needs more bus routes. A transport survey found that one in three residents now skips evening events because the last bus stops at eight. Honestly, the whole system looks out of date to me.
guiada.feedback: La evidencia es el dato verificable de la encuesta de transporte; lo demás son opiniones sobre lo que «debería» hacerse.
guiada.pista: La evidencia se puede comprobar; la opinión suele empezar por I feel u Honestly.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Las cifras de la encuesta respaldan la tesis de que más gente va en bicicleta.»
guiada.texto: The survey figures ___ the claim that more people now cycle to work, since fewer cars crossed the bridge this spring.
guiada.feedback: Figures support a claim cuando aportan datos que la refuerzan; back o bear out también encajan.
guiada.pista: Verbo que significa «respaldar»; empieza por s.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Una objeción es que el puente es demasiado estrecho.»
guiada.respuesta: One objection is that the bridge is too narrow
guiada.feedback: La objeción presenta el argumento contrario con One objection is that…, seguida de una frase completa.
guiada.pista: Empieza por One objection y sigue con that.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige cómo responde la hablante a la objeción de los padres.
practica.audio: Our claim is simple: schools should start at nine. The evidence comes from a sleep study of six hundred teenagers, who did better in morning tests after a later start. Some parents raise an objection, saying that later finishes would disrupt sport. The rebuttal is that clubs can move to the lunch break, when every pupil is free.
opciones: By proposing that clubs meet during the lunch break.
By showing that teenagers sleep better before an early morning match.
By admitting that sport matters more than morning tests ever do.
practica.feedback: La réplica a la objeción de los padres es trasladar los clubes a la hora de la comida; el resto no se dice.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase del debate con la pieza del argumento que representa.
pares: A survey of nine hundred parents found that most prefer later starts
Evidencia comprobable
I honestly feel that mornings are simply too early
Opinión personal
Our claim is that the school day should start later
Tesis que se defiende
One objection is that parents would finish work earlier
Objeción del otro lado
The rebuttal is that clubs could meet at the lunch break
Réplica a la objeción
practica.feedback: Cada frase cumple un papel distinto: el dato comprobable es evidencia, la sensación personal es opinión, y tesis, objeción y réplica ocupan su lugar.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué hace la hablante con la afirmación del municipio?
opciones: She casts doubt on it by noting that its evidence is too thin.
She backs it while asking for a longer trial period.
She rebuts it with a new survey of the library's users.
She accepts it but objects to Monday as the closing day.
practica.texto: The council claims that closing the library on Mondays will save money. The figures it published, however, cover only one month, and they ignore the cost of extra staff elsewhere. A single month is hardly a representative sample, so the claim remains weak.
practica.feedback: Señala que un solo mes no es una muestra representativa: pone en duda la afirmación sin aportar datos propios ni aceptarla.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el debate y elige qué objeción plantea Leo a la tesis de Sara.
evaluacion.audio: At the youth council, Sara opened by putting forward a claim: schools should stop setting homework at weekends. Her evidence came from a survey of eight hundred pupils, most of whom said they slept badly on Sunday nights. Leo raised an objection. In his opinion, weekend homework teaches good habits, and he had seen it work for his cousins. Sara answered that a story about cousins is not hard evidence, and that her sample was representative because it covered twelve schools. Leo conceded that the survey was larger than anything he could offer, but he still wanted some kind of weekly task.
opciones: That weekend homework builds good habits, as he has seen in his family.
That the survey asked too few pupils in too few of the schools.
That pupils who sleep badly need less homework all week.
That Sara's claim came from an opinion rather than evidence.
evaluacion.feedback: Leo basa su objeción en los buenos hábitos que, según él, enseña la tarea de fin de semana; la crítica a la muestra o a la opinión es de Sara, no suya.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué sugiere Sara al responder sobre los primos de Leo?
evaluacion.audio: At the youth council, Sara opened by putting forward a claim: schools should stop setting homework at weekends. Her evidence came from a survey of eight hundred pupils, most of whom said they slept badly on Sunday nights. Leo raised an objection. In his opinion, weekend homework teaches good habits, and he had seen it work for his cousins. Sara answered that a story about cousins is not hard evidence, and that her sample was representative because it covered twelve schools. Leo conceded that the survey was larger than anything he could offer, but he still wanted some kind of weekly task.
opciones: That a personal story cannot replace evidence from a wide sample.
That his cousins are less able than the pupils in the survey.
That weekend homework could not possibly suit any pupil.
That Leo should have surveyed his cousins' school himself.
evaluacion.feedback: Sara dice que una historia sobre primos no es evidencia sólida y defiende su muestra amplia: sugiere que una anécdota no sustituye a los datos.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Una sola reseña es una anécdota, no una prueba sólida.»
evaluacion.texto: A single excellent review is an anecdote, not hard ___. It cannot stand for the thousands of customers who never wrote one.
evaluacion.feedback: Hard evidence es la colocación para pruebas sólidas y comprobables; una anécdota aislada no lo es.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe la tesis y la evidencia de este debate sobre los museos.
evaluacion.texto: Debate: ¿deben los museos ser gratuitos? Tu tesis: sí. Tu evidencia: según una encuesta, el 72 % de los visitantes volvería más a menudo si la entrada no costara nada.
evaluacion.respuesta: My claim is that museums should be free. According to a survey, seventy-two per cent of visitors would return more often if entry cost nothing.
aceptadas: I am arguing that museums should be free of charge. The survey found that 72 per cent of visitors would come back more often if there were no entry fee.

evidencias: museums should be free of charge

evaluacion.feedback: Una buena respuesta separa la tesis (My claim is that…) de la evidencia con su fuente (According to…) y su dato.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué sugiere Tom con su réplica sobre quienes dudan de la encuesta?
opciones: That anyone who doubts it must now produce evidence of their own.
That agreement with earlier surveys makes the small sample irrelevant.
That people who doubt it are acting in bad faith and should be ignored.
That he will run a larger survey next year to settle the matter.
repaso.texto: Tom's rebuttal was brief. He admitted that the survey had reached only two hundred people, but pointed out that its results matched every earlier survey in the region, which would be strange if they were an accident. He did not claim certainty; he suggested only that those who doubted the figures should now produce evidence of their own.
repaso.feedback: Tom admite la limitación de la muestra y sugiere que quien duda debe aportar sus propias pruebas; no dice que el tamaño sea irrelevante, ni acusa de mala fe, ni anuncia otra encuesta.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Eso puede poner en duda la tesis, aunque no la destruye.»
repaso.texto: The figures in the report cover only one week. That alone may ___ doubt on the claim, although it does not ruin it.
repaso.feedback: Cast doubt on es la colocación para poner en duda una afirmación; throw doubt on es una variante menos frecuente.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige qué opina la hablante de la réplica de los organizadores.
repaso.audio: Some neighbours object that a Sunday market would be noisy. The organisers reply that it would close at two, long before the evening. I think that answer deals with the worry, though I would still like some hard evidence about the noise before the council votes.
opciones: It answers the concern, but she wants facts about the noise.
It answers the concern so well that no further checks are needed.
It is reasonable, although she doubts that the market would close at two.
It is a fair reply, but she thinks the organisers should pay for noise monitors.
repaso.feedback: La hablante acepta la réplica como respuesta al problema, pero pide pruebas sobre el ruido antes de la votación; no dice que sobren las comprobaciones ni duda del horario ni reclama que paguen los organizadores.

classes.objetivo: Rebatir con tacto y firmeza usando atenuantes, refuerzos y frases hendidas en un texto argumentativo.

ensenanza.en: What matters is the cost of the new benches, and it is the cost that many families overlook.
ensenanza.es: Lo que importa es el coste de los bancos nuevos, y es el coste lo que muchas familias pasan por alto.
ensenanza.nota: Frase hendida con What…is y con It is…that: las dos colocan el coste en primer plano.

ensenanza.en: The plan is arguably the cheapest option, but it is by no means the fairest for families with three children.
ensenanza.es: El plan es posiblemente la opción más barata, pero de ningún modo es la más justa para las familias con tres hijos.
ensenanza.nota: Arguably atenúa (no puedes probarlo); by no means refuerza la negación. Son dos matices distintos.

ensenanza.en: That is a reasonable point, yet I have reservations about the timing, which could hardly be worse for shopkeepers.
ensenanza.es: Es un punto razonable, pero tengo reservas sobre el momento elegido, que no podría ser peor para los comerciantes.
ensenanza.nota: Concede (reasonable point) y rebate con tacto: have reservations about suaviza un desacuerdo real.

ensenanza.en: The fee is undoubtedly a problem for large families, and far from easing the burden, the plan would increase it.
ensenanza.es: La cuota es sin duda un problema para las familias numerosas y, lejos de aliviar la carga, el plan la aumentaría.
ensenanza.nota: Undoubtedly refuerza lo que sí sostienes; far from + -ing equivale a «lejos de» y introduce lo contrario de lo esperado.

ensenanza.en: To a large degree the dispute is about trust, and what is essential is a fair price for every family.
ensenanza.es: En gran medida la disputa trata de la confianza, y lo esencial es un precio justo para cada familia.
ensenanza.nota: To a large degree es un atenuante de cantidad; What is essential is… es otra frase hendida con What.

ensenanza.en: Councillors who oppose the plan should drive the point home calmly, because a raised voice rarely wins a neighbourhood debate.
ensenanza.es: Los concejales que se oponen al plan deberían dejarlo bien claro con calma, porque levantar la voz rara vez gana un debate vecinal.
ensenanza.nota: Drive the point home = dejar algo bien claro; el tono sereno también es un recurso de firmeza.

explicacion.texto: Para rebatir sin sonar agresivo, concede primero y luego combina tres recursos. Atenúa lo que no puedes probar con arguably, to a large degree o I have reservations about…; refuerza lo que sí sostienes con undoubtedly, clearly o by no means; y destaca lo importante con una frase hendida: What matters is… («lo que importa es…») o It is the cost that… («es el coste lo que…»). No mezcles atenuación y refuerzo en la misma afirmación, y recuerda que tras It is + elemento va that, no what.

formula.nota: concesión: reconoces algo al otro lado

formula.texto: but what matters is the cost.
formula.nota: frase hendida con What…is para destacar

formula.texto: It is the cost that families overlook.

filas.texto: It is the price that worries us.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: It is the cost what worries me, not the design.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: It is the cost that worries me, not the design.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En español se dice «es el coste lo que me preocupa», pero en inglés, tras It is + elemento, se usa that.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Is the cost that worries me most.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: It is the cost that worries me most.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: El español omite el sujeto («es el coste lo que…»), pero en inglés la frase hendida necesita It delante de is.

situacion.contexto: Ana defiende la cuota del club deportivo del colegio y Leo la rebate con tacto.

dialogo.texto: I think the club fee is fair. It is arguably the lowest in town.
dialogo.traduccion: Creo que la cuota del club es justa. Es posiblemente la más baja de la ciudad.

dialogo.texto: That is a reasonable point, but what matters is the cost for families.
dialogo.traduccion: Es un punto razonable, pero lo que importa es el coste para las familias.

dialogo.texto: But the club needs the money.
dialogo.traduccion: Pero el club necesita el dinero.

dialogo.texto: I agree. However, it is the cost for families that the club overlooks, and it is undoubtedly too high for some.
dialogo.traduccion: Estoy de acuerdo. Sin embargo, es el coste para las familias lo que el club pasa por alto, y sin duda es demasiado alto para algunas.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué dice Leo que el club pasa por alto?

opciones.es: La necesidad de dinero del club.
El precio más bajo de la ciudad.

item.feedback: Leo dice «it is the cost for families that the club overlooks»: la frase hendida destaca el coste.

guiada.consigna: Elige la frase hendida que destaca «el tráfico» como lo que molesta a los vecinos.
opciones: It is the traffic that bothers most of the neighbours.
The traffic is bothering most of the neighbours.
It is the traffic what bothers most of the neighbours.
guiada.feedback: La hendida con It is + elemento + that pone el tráfico en primer plano; tras el elemento destacado no se usa what.
guiada.pista: Busca It is + lo destacado + that + verbo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «El plan es posiblemente la opción más barata, aunque no puedo demostrarlo.»
guiada.texto: The council's figures are still incomplete. The plan is ___ the cheapest option, although I cannot prove it.
guiada.feedback: Arguably atenúa una afirmación que no puedes probar; undoubtedly la reforzaría y contradiría «I cannot prove it».
guiada.pista: Adverbio de cautela; empieza por a.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Lo que importa a los vecinos es el ruido por la noche.»
guiada.respuesta: What matters to the neighbours is the noise at night
aceptadas: The noise at night is what matters to the neighbours
guiada.feedback: What + sujeto + verbo + is + X: la hendida con What coloca el ruido por la noche como lo destacado.
guiada.pista: Empieza por What matters y cierra con is + lo importante.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige la postura de la hablante ante el plan.
practica.audio: Councillors are undoubtedly under pressure, and I have reservations about the timing. The plan is by no means perfect, but it is arguably the best we have. What matters now is that residents can see the figures before they vote.
opciones: She backs the plan cautiously and wants the figures published.
She is convinced the plan is flawed and wants the vote cancelled.
She accepts the plan as it stands and sees no need for more information.
practica.feedback: La hablante tiene reservas, pero considera el plan «arguably the best we have» y pide ver las cifras antes de votar: apoyo cauteloso, ni rechazo ni confianza total.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué afirma el autor sin ninguna reserva en este fragmento?
opciones: That the new cycle lane is popular among local people.
That the lane has reduced the number of accidents.
That the lane may eventually save the council some money.
That the road now feels safer to every cyclist.
practica.texto: Our new cycle lane is undoubtedly popular, but the claim that it has cut accidents is harder to prove. It has arguably made the road feel safer, and far from being a waste of money, it may even save some, although nobody can say by how much.
practica.feedback: Undoubtedly refuerza la popularidad del carril; las demás afirmaciones van atenuadas (harder to prove, arguably, may, nobody can say).

practica.consigna: Reformula con una frase hendida que empiece por What.
practica.respuesta: What worries the residents is the price.
aceptadas: What concerns the residents is the price.
What bothers the residents is the price.
What troubles the residents is the price.
practica.feedback: What + verbo + sujeto + is + X convierte the price en lo destacado de la frase.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha el fragmento y elige cómo se dirige Carlos a Mia al rebatir su propuesta.
evaluacion.audio: Carlos got up at the residents' meeting to answer Mia's proposal for a parking charge. He began by conceding that she had a reasonable point: the street really is crowded at weekends. Then he chose his words with care. The plan is arguably the simplest option, he said, but it is by no means the fairest, because it is the cost that families with two cars will overlook until the first bill arrives. He added that he had reservations about the timing, since a charge introduced in January would hit people who had just paid for the holidays. He never raised his voice. He simply repeated, calmly, that what matters is that nobody is priced out of their own street.
opciones: Politely, acknowledging her point before he goes on to disagree.
Firmly, but only about the timing, since he accepts the charge in principle.
Cautiously, agreeing with her while hoping she will drop the proposal.
Emotionally, appealing to the neighbours' anger rather than to the facts.
evaluacion.feedback: Carlos empieza concediendo que Mia tiene un punto razonable y solo después rebate, con tono sereno: cortesía sin perder firmeza; no acepta el cobro en principio ni apela a la ira de los vecinos.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué sugiere Carlos sobre las familias con dos autos?
evaluacion.audio: Carlos got up at the residents' meeting to answer Mia's proposal for a parking charge. He began by conceding that she had a reasonable point: the street really is crowded at weekends. Then he chose his words with care. The plan is arguably the simplest option, he said, but it is by no means the fairest, because it is the cost that families with two cars will overlook until the first bill arrives. He added that he had reservations about the timing, since a charge introduced in January would hit people who had just paid for the holidays. He never raised his voice. He simply repeated, calmly, that what matters is that nobody is priced out of their own street.
opciones: That some households would only discover the burden when the bills arrive.
That families with one car would pay nothing at all.
That Mia has hidden the real cost from the residents on purpose.
That the shops on the street would lose customers because of the charge.
evaluacion.feedback: Carlos dice que las familias con dos autos pasarán por alto el coste hasta recibir la primera factura: sugiere un impacto que muchos no anticipan; no acusa a Mia, no habla de comercios ni promete gratuidad a nadie.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Lejos de aliviar el problema, el cobro lo trasladaría a la calle siguiente.»
evaluacion.texto: Everyone agrees that parking is a problem. The real difficulty is that ___ from easing it, the charge would simply move it to the next street.
evaluacion.feedback: Far from + -ing introduce lo contrario de lo esperado: el cobro no alivia, desplaza el problema.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe tu intervención: concesión, refutación con frase hendida y cierre.
evaluacion.texto: Debate escolar: ¿deben los alumnos limpiar su aula una vez por semana? Defiendes que sí. Escribe unas 190–250 palabras: concede que se pierde tiempo de clase; rebate con frases hendidas (What matters is…; It is the cost that…); usa un atenuante (arguably) y un refuerzo (undoubtedly); y cierra con una conclusión.
evaluacion.respuesta: In my view, pupils should clean their own classroom once a week. Admittedly, it takes time away from lessons, and I have reservations about how often we can do it during exams. That is a reasonable point, but what matters is the habit we build: it is the pupils who use the room every day who should look after it, and it is undoubtedly fairer that everyone shares the work. Arguably, a clean room also helps us study, because nobody concentrates well among rubbish. Far from being a burden, ten minutes on Friday is a small price to pay. It is the cost of extra staff that the school would carry otherwise, and that money could buy books instead. To a large degree, the question is about respect, and what is essential is that we treat the classroom as ours. To conclude, a tidy room by no means needs a cleaner, only a rota.
aceptadas: I believe that pupils should clean their classroom every week. I concede that it takes time from lessons, and some parents think the school should do it. That is a valid point, but what counts is the habit we learn. It is the pupils who use the room all day, so it is undoubtedly fair that we look after it. Arguably, a clean room helps us study, because nobody concentrates well among rubbish. It is also the cost that the school would save, and that money could buy books for the library. Far from being unfair, ten minutes on Friday is a small price to pay. To a large degree this is a question of respect, and what is essential is that we share the work, because the classroom belongs to all of us. In conclusion, the whole class benefits, and nobody is asked to do more than a fair share.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena intervención concede antes de rebatir, usa al menos una frase hendida, equilibra atenuantes y refuerzos y cierra con una conclusión.

repaso.consigna: ¿Con qué actitud escribe la remitente esta respuesta al municipio?
opciones: Polite, but firm that the council's silence was the real problem.
Apologetic, accepting that residents had read the old rule wrongly.
Hostile, blaming the council for writing a confusing rule.
Neutral, merely reporting what other residents have said.
repaso.texto: Dear Councillor, thank you for your reply. You are right that the old rule was hard to follow, and we are grateful for your patience. That said, what worries the residents is not the wording but the silence that followed: it is the lack of any answer that has cost the council their trust.
repaso.feedback: Agradece y concede que la norma era difícil, pero con «That said» desplaza el problema al silencio del municipio: cortesía con firmeza.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Es el momento elegido lo que el municipio pasa por alto.»
repaso.respuesta: It is the timing that the council overlooks
repaso.feedback: It is + elemento + that + resto: la hendida coloca the timing como lo destacado.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Tengo reservas sobre el momento elegido y quisiera más tiempo para estudiarlo.»
repaso.texto: Mia's proposal is reasonable and well meant. I do, however, have ___ about the timing, and I would like more time to study it.
repaso.feedback: Have reservations about es la fórmula tactful para expresar un desacuerdo moderado; doubts o concerns también encajan.

classes.objetivo: Defender una postura en un debate vecinal integrando tesis, argumentos, concesión, refutación enfática y conclusión.

ensenanza.en: As a resident with a vested interest, I argue that the park should stay open until ten, and I will give two reasons.
ensenanza.es: Como vecino con un interés personal en juego, sostengo que el parque debería seguir abierto hasta las diez, y daré dos razones.
ensenanza.nota: Declarar tu interés (a vested interest) es honesto y refuerza la tesis: la tesis va al principio.

ensenanza.en: Neighbours can launch a petition; four hundred signatures show that they want to have a say, and the council must listen.
ensenanza.es: Los vecinos pueden lanzar una recogida de firmas; cuatrocientas firmas muestran que quieren tener voz, y el municipio debe escuchar.
ensenanza.nota: Launch a petition + have a say: el primer argumento se apoya en evidencia que se puede contar.

ensenanza.en: Much as I understand the rubbish problem, families need a safe place, and that should not come at the expense of the children.
ensenanza.es: Por mucho que entienda el problema de la basura, las familias necesitan un lugar seguro, y eso no debe ir a costa de los niños.
ensenanza.nota: Concesión con Much as + refutación; at the expense of = a costa de, útil para señalar quién pierde.

ensenanza.en: Noise is the real sticking point for the houses beside the playground, and I concede that it deserves a serious hearing.
ensenanza.es: El ruido es el verdadero punto de fricción para las casas junto a la zona de juegos, y reconozco que merece una audiencia seria.
ensenanza.nota: A sticking point es el obstáculo principal de una negociación; conceder lo que es fuerte da credibilidad.

ensenanza.en: When the plan is put to a vote, the council should hear both sides first, and every resident should be allowed to speak.
ensenanza.es: Cuando el plan se someta a votación, el municipio debería escuchar primero a ambas partes y dejar hablar a cada vecino.
ensenanza.nota: Put to a vote (voz pasiva) y hear both sides describen un proceso justo antes de decidir.

ensenanza.en: To conclude, the council and the neighbours can reach a compromise: longer hours, a weekend cleaning team and quiet after nine.
ensenanza.es: Para concluir, el municipio y los vecinos pueden llegar a un acuerdo: más horas, un equipo de limpieza los fines de semana y silencio después de las nueve.
ensenanza.nota: La conclusión cierra con un acuerdo concreto: reach a compromise = llegar a un término medio.

explicacion.titulo: Debate vecinal: todo el bloque junto
explicacion.texto: En un debate vecinal encadenas lo aprendido en el bloque: tesis (My position is that…), dos argumentos con evidencia (First…, According to…), una concesión (Admittedly…, Much as I…) seguida de una refutación (nevertheless, what matters is…, it is… that…) y una conclusión con un acuerdo (To conclude, we can reach a compromise…). Declarar un interés personal y escuchar a ambas partes da credibilidad. Varía el tono con arguably y undoubtedly. Escucha primero qué concede el otro: así sabrás cuál es su verdadera objeción y podrás responderla con precisión.

formula.texto: My position is that the park should open later.
formula.nota: tesis: tu postura desde el principio

formula.texto: Much as I understand the rubbish problem,
what matters is that families have a safe place.
To conclude, a compromise is possible.

filas.texto: What matters is… / It is… that…

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: As a conclusion, I support the petition.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: To conclude, I support the petition.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Calco de «como conclusión»: para cerrar se dice To conclude o In conclusion, no as a conclusion.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Although the park has rubbish, however the residents use it.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Although the park has rubbish, the residents use it.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Although ya marca el contraste; no se añade however en la segunda parte, igual que no se suma but.

situacion.contexto: Carlos y Ana debaten en la reunión del barrio cuándo debe cerrar el parque.

dialogo.texto: My position is that the park should close at eight, because of the noise.
dialogo.traduccion: Mi postura es que el parque debería cerrar a las ocho, por el ruido.

dialogo.texto: Much as I understand the noise problem, what matters is that families have a safe place in the evening.
dialogo.traduccion: Por mucho que entienda el problema del ruido, lo que importa es que las familias tengan un lugar seguro por la tarde.

dialogo.texto: Admittedly, the playground is busy. Nevertheless, the residents near the park cannot sleep.
dialogo.traduccion: Es cierto que la zona de juegos está concurrida. Sin embargo, los vecinos cercanos al parque no pueden dormir.

dialogo.texto: To conclude, let us find a compromise: open until ten, with a quiet rule after nine.
dialogo.traduccion: Para concluir, busquemos un acuerdo: abierto hasta las diez, con una norma de silencio después de las nueve.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué acuerdo propone Ana?

opciones.es: Abrir hasta las diez, con silencio desde las nueve.
Cerrar el parque a las ocho.
Abrir el parque toda la noche.

item.feedback: Ana propone «open until ten, with a quiet rule after nine»: un término medio entre ambas posturas.

guiada.consigna: Localiza la tesis: ¿cuál es la afirmación central del discurso?
opciones: The old tennis courts should be repaired and reopened, not replaced.
Many neighbours asked why the speaker opposes the car park.
The council deserves thanks for listening to its residents.
guiada.texto: Good evening, neighbours. Many of you have asked me why I oppose the car park. I will keep my answer short: the old tennis courts should be repaired and reopened, not replaced. I will give two reasons, but first let me thank the council for listening.
guiada.feedback: La tesis llega tras la pregunta de los vecinos: las pistas deben repararse y reabrirse; el agradecimiento y la pregunta son solo contexto.
guiada.pista: La tesis es lo que defiende, no lo que agradece ni lo que le han preguntado.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Antes de votar, el municipio prometió escuchar a ambas partes.»
guiada.texto: The car park plan has divided the town. Before anyone casts a vote, the council has promised to ___ both sides of the argument.
guiada.feedback: Hear both sides es la colocación para dar voz a las dos posturas antes de decidir.
guiada.pista: Verbo de percepción auditiva; empieza por h.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Por mucho que respete la petición, no puedo apoyarla.»
guiada.respuesta: Much as I respect the petition I cannot support it
aceptadas: I cannot support it much as I respect the petition
guiada.feedback: Much as I respect… concede el valor de la petición y la postura propia llega después, sin but; la concesión también puede ir al final.
guiada.pista: Empieza por Much as y no añadas but.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué concede la vecina antes de refutar.
practica.audio: I have lived beside this playground for twenty years. Admittedly, the noise can be tiring, and I have reservations about the late opening hours. But what matters is that children have somewhere safe to play, and it is the council that should manage the rubbish and the noise, not the families who use the park.
opciones: That the noise from the playground can be tiring.
That the council already manages the rubbish badly.
That the families are the cause of the noise.
practica.feedback: «Admittedly, the noise can be tiring» es la concesión; «But what matters is…» abre su refutación.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase del debate con su paso en la estructura.
pares: My position is that the car park should go elsewhere
Tesis
The petition has six hundred signatures
Argumento con evidencia
Admittedly, drivers need a place to park
Concesión
What matters is that the courts stay open to everyone
Refutación enfática
To conclude, we can reach a compromise
Conclusión con acuerdo
practica.feedback: Cada frase ocupa un lugar del debate: la tesis abre, la evidencia apoya, la concesión reconoce, la refutación enfatiza y la conclusión cierra.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué sugiere la autora sobre su voto en esta carta a los vecinos?
opciones: That she is still unsure and wants to listen before committing.
That she has already decided against the plan but will not say so.
That she will follow the majority whatever her own view may be.
That she expects the vote to be cancelled before March.
practica.texto: Dear neighbours, thank you for your messages. I cannot promise that the car park will go ahead, and I will not pretend that every objection has an easy answer. All I can say is that a vote will be held in March, and that I shall not vote until I have heard from residents on both sides.
practica.feedback: Dice que no puede prometer nada y que no votará antes de escuchar a los vecinos de ambas posturas: está indecisa y abierta a escuchar.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha la reunión y elige qué actitud muestra Mar ante el compromiso de Tom.
evaluacion.audio: Sol chaired the meeting about the old tennis courts. Mar spoke first and put forward her thesis: the courts should become a community garden. Her evidence was a petition with five hundred signatures. Tom, who has a vested interest because he trains there on Saturdays, conceded that a garden would look lovely, but what matters to him is that teenagers have a place to play. He proposed a compromise: half the land for vegetables, half for the courts. Mar did not accept at once. She said she would need to hear both sides of the club first, although she admitted that half a garden was better than none. Sol then put the idea to a vote.
opciones: Open to it, though not ready to accept it on the spot.
Supportive, but only if Tom gives up his Saturday training sessions.
Opposed, rejecting any change to her original proposal for the garden.
Neutral, leaving the whole decision to the club.
evaluacion.feedback: Mar no acepta «at once» y quiere escuchar al club, pero admite que media huerta es mejor que nada: apertura con cautela; no pone condiciones a Tom, no rechaza todo cambio ni se desentiende.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha de nuevo: ¿por qué menciona el narrador que Tom tiene «a vested interest»?
evaluacion.audio: Sol chaired the meeting about the old tennis courts. Mar spoke first and put forward her thesis: the courts should become a community garden. Her evidence was a petition with five hundred signatures. Tom, who has a vested interest because he trains there on Saturdays, conceded that a garden would look lovely, but what matters to him is that teenagers have a place to play. He proposed a compromise: half the land for vegetables, half for the courts. Mar did not accept at once. She said she would need to hear both sides of the club first, although she admitted that half a garden was better than none. Sol then put the idea to a vote.
opciones: To suggest that his view may reflect his own use of the courts.
To show that Tom has the legal power to stop the garden.
To explain why Tom collected the five hundred signatures.
To hint that Mar herself has no interest in the old courts at all.
evaluacion.feedback: El narrador explica que Tom entrena allí los sábados: su postura puede estar influida por su propio interés; no colecta firmas ni tiene poder legal.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Los vecinos decidieron lanzar una recogida de firmas.»
evaluacion.texto: Unhappy with the plan, the neighbours decided to ___ a petition that any resident could sign. Within a week it had four hundred signatures, and the council had to reply.
evaluacion.feedback: Launch a petition es la colocación habitual para iniciar una recogida de firmas; start o organise también encajan.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe tu intervención en el debate del parque, de la tesis a la conclusión.
evaluacion.texto: Debate vecinal: ¿debe el parque abrir hasta las diez de la noche? Defiendes que sí. Escribe unas 210–270 palabras con: tesis; dos argumentos (una petición con 400 firmas y que no hay otra zona de juegos); una concesión sobre el ruido y la basura; una refutación con frase hendida; y una conclusión con un acuerdo (silencio desde las nueve).
evaluacion.respuesta: As a resident, my position is that the park should stay open until ten at night. First, the petition has four hundred signatures, which shows that many neighbours want a say and want longer hours. Second, there is no other playground in this area, so families have nowhere else to go after work. Admittedly, there is some noise and rubbish after the weekend, and I have reservations about the late hours for the people who live next to the park. Much as I understand their tiredness, what matters is that children and parents have a safe place in the evening. It is the council that should clean the park and watch the noise, not the families who use it, and that should not come at the expense of the children. Arguably, closing at eight would solve one problem and create a bigger one. To conclude, we can reach a compromise: the park opens until ten, with a quiet rule after nine, and the council puts the plan to a vote.
aceptadas: In my view, the park should remain open until ten at night. First, the petition has 400 signatures, so the residents clearly want longer hours and a say in the decision. Second, there is no other playground nearby, and families need somewhere safe to go after work. Much as I understand the noise problem, what matters is that children and parents have a safe place in the evening. I concede that there is some rubbish at weekends; nevertheless, it is the council that must keep the park clean, not the families who use it. Arguably, closing earlier would only move the problem somewhere else, and it would happen at the expense of the children. To conclude, a compromise is possible: the park stays open until ten, with silence after nine, and the plan goes to a vote.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena intervención tiene tesis, dos argumentos con evidencia, concesión, refutación enfática y una conclusión con acuerdo.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender el comunicado del municipio?
opciones: That the council means to delay a decision without backing either side.
That the council has quietly decided to reject the petition.
That the eleven letters will outweigh the signed petition.
That residents will be able to vote on the park hours in spring.
repaso.texto: The council has received 412 signatures calling for longer park hours and eleven letters opposing them. Officials say they will take every view into account, and that no decision will be made before the spring. Residents who hoped for a quick answer were not reassured; one of them called the statement a polite way of doing nothing.
repaso.feedback: «Take every view into account» y «no decision before the spring» sugieren aplazar sin comprometerse; por eso un vecino lo llama «a polite way of doing nothing».

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Es el municipio quien debe ofrecer un lugar seguro.»
repaso.respuesta: It is the council that must provide a safe place
repaso.feedback: It is + elemento + that: la hendida pone al municipio como responsable.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Aún pueden llegar a un acuerdo antes de la votación.»
repaso.texto: The two sides have little in common, but they may still ___ a compromise before the vote takes place next month.
repaso.feedback: Reach a compromise es la colocación habitual; find o strike a compromise también son naturales.

notes: Claves verificadas contra texto/audio en las 5 clases; una sola respuesta defendible por ítem.
c21 g0, c22 p0, c23 e1/r0/r2, c24 p0/e0/e1, c25 e0/p2 (y e2): distractores reescritos como casi-aciertos (propuesta vs concesión, generalización excesiva, actitud invertida, cierto pero no dicho).
c25 p2: texto ajustado para que la inferencia «indecisa» sea inequívoca; c25 e2: contexto que excluye «sign a petition»; c24 e1: consigna corregida (pregunta por las familias con dos autos).
aceptadas ampliadas (agree, give, fooled, prove, shed, presumably, hammer out, etc.); rúbricas c22 e3 con variantes.
Léxico C1 real (colocaciones), sin relleno B1 nuevo; ≥2 ítems de inferencia/actitud/propósito por clase; sin etiquetas de hablante.
